risks.title: Persistent Inflationary Pressures
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated above central bank targets, driven by supply shocks in energy and other sectors, as well as ongoing effects of tariffs. This necessitates a careful balancing act for policymakers.
risks.watch_for: July and August CPI and PPI data releases, Federal Reserve's assessment of inflation trends in FOMC statements and minutes.

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Commodity Disruptions
risks.summary: Ongoing conflicts, particularly in the Middle East, are leading to sharp increases in energy prices and prolonged disruptions to supply chains for key commodities, exacerbating inflationary pressures and global economic uncertainty.
risks.watch_for: Developments in the Middle East conflict, oil price fluctuations, and reports on supply chain resilience.

risks.title: Monetary Policy Uncertainty and Divergence
risks.summary: The Federal Reserve faces a challenging path, with some officials favoring rate hikes while the majority holds rates steady. This divergence creates uncertainty about the future direction of monetary policy and its impact on markets.
risks.watch_for: FOMC meeting minutes, statements, and economic projections; dissenting votes within the FOMC.
sources: Kraken Blog (July jobs, CPI, and Fed minutes headline two weeks of catalysts, August 05, 2026)
Asia Times (Brace for higher US interest rates from the Fed, August 05, 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Productivity Lag
risks.summary: The significant investment in AI is a key driver of growth, but concerns are rising about its sustainability and whether it will translate into broad-based productivity gains or remain an isolated source of expansion.
risks.watch_for: Corporate capital expenditure plans for AI, productivity growth data, and reports on AI adoption across sectors.
sources: Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20, 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 13, 2026)

risks.title: Elevated US National Debt and Fiscal Space
risks.summary: US federal debt has surpassed the size of the economy, limiting fiscal room to maneuver during future shocks. Rising debt service costs and a commitment to increased defense spending add to fiscal pressures.
risks.watch_for: CBO's budget deficit and debt projections, Congressional budget proposals, and discussions on fiscal sustainability.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 13, 2026)
Congressional Budget Office (Outlook for the Budget and the Economy, February 01, 2026)
KPMG (The two faces of the economy, January 12, 2026)

risks.title: Tariff Impacts and Trade Policy Uncertainty
risks.summary: New and existing tariffs continue to affect import costs and trade flows, contributing to inflationary pressures. Uncertainty surrounding future trade policies adds to business caution and can disrupt supply chains.
risks.watch_for: Announcements of new tariffs, trade data releases, and statements from trade organizations.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (Outlook for the Budget and the Economy, February 01, 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Dynamics and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: While the labor market shows resilience with low unemployment, concerns persist about low labor turnover, limited job opportunities for new entrants, and the impact of AI on hiring. Affordability remains a key issue for consumers.
risks.watch_for: July jobs report, wage growth data, quit rates, and consumer sentiment surveys.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, March 13, 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (July 2026 Economic Outlook and Key Themes, July 20, 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (The U.S. economy in 2026: What to watch for, March 13, 2026)

risks.title: Potential for Stock Market Volatility
risks.summary: Market volatility is expected due to domestic and international political uncertainties, alongside concerns about AI infrastructure spending and tech stock valuations. Geopolitical risks, such as those related to Iran, can also trigger sharp market movements.
risks.watch_for: S&P 500 performance, VIX index, and news related to geopolitical events and corporate earnings.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook: Keeping discipline in noisy markets, August 03, 2026)
Guggenheim Investments (Strong Earnings Outweighed by Worries Around Higher Oil and Interest Rates, July 27, 2026)

consensus_note: There is a broad consensus that persistent inflation, driven by supply shocks and geopolitical tensions, remains a primary concern. While AI investment is seen as a growth engine, its long-term productivity impact is debated. Disagreement exists on the pace and direction of monetary policy, with some FOMC members advocating for rate hikes while others maintain a hold stance.
